title: mail-parser sender address extraction can trust sender-controlled header text
summary: get_server_ipaddress() can misidentify sender-controlled text as a sender IP address. The fix selects candidates by header position and stops at a trusted hop that supplies no usable address.

severity.rationale: The flaw affects integrity of sender attribution in mail-processing integrations. Exposure depends on a consumer trusting this helper for a security decision, limiting the direct impact to that integration.

exposure: Agent mail tools that use get_server_ipaddress() for sender attribution need review. Parsing mail alone does not establish that the returned address controls a security decision.

remediation.action: Upgrade and handle unknown sender addresses
remediation.details: Use mail-parser 4.6.2 or later. Until upgraded, derive attribution from authenticated signals outside this library instead of trusting get_server_ipaddress().
remediation.risk: The helper now returns None for ambiguous bare addresses and trusted hops without addresses; callers must handle it.

verification: Confirm mail-parser is 4.6.2 or later and that callers handle None without treating it as a trusted sender.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
